finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller that reaches the handler with a user in the request context can run purgeAll(). rotateKeys, by contrast, correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated, non-admin user sending an HTTP request to the purge endpoint. The user comes from the request context via userFrom(r).

trace.note: purge handler entry; the route registration is not present in the repo
u := userFrom(r) fetches the user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, so there is no early return or 403

finding.guards_checked: The repo contains only handlers.go, so I could not see any route registration or auth middleware that might restrict /purge to admins. The only guard in the handler is checkPerm, and its result is ignored. The mustPerm pattern used in rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 is absent here. userFrom at handlers.go:40 does an unchecked type assertion, so a request with no authenticated user panics. That is a robustness issue rather than a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm(u, "admin") at handlers.go:26 returns a bool that is discarded. No other guard exists in the repo. The route registration and any middleware are not present.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14, which only returns a bool) as a bare statement, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user in the context. rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 returns on a failed mustPerm, which shows the intended pattern. Every trace line matches the candidate's description. The only residual uncertainty is an unseen upstream admin-only middleware, which would be defense in depth and doesn't make this handler's check work.
